title: Germany raises its cyber threat rating to 'tense to critical', citing fast AI growth
excerpt: Germany's federal cyber security office says attackers now exploit new flaws within days, and expects more attacks run by autonomous AI agents.

sources.title: BSI: BSI-Jahreslagebericht: Cybersicherheitslage in Deutschland ist angespannt bis kritisch
ZDFheute: BSI-Lagebericht sieht höhere Gefahr für Cyberangriffe wegen KI
The News (Reuters): Germany elevates agentic AI threat levels 'tense to critical'

body_html:
Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), the national agency responsible for cyber security, has raised its overall assessment of the country's cyber threat level from "tense" to "tense to critical". The change was announced on 19 November 2026, when the BSI presented its annual report on the state of IT security in Germany together with the Federal Interior Minister, Alexander Dobrindt.

In its press release, the BSI gives two reasons for the higher rating: the geopolitical situation and the rapid development of artificial intelligence.

What the report says

The BSI's figures describe a shrinking window between a software flaw becoming known and attackers using it:

  • About 160 new software vulnerabilities were recorded per day, an increase of 35 percent.
  • The time until a newly known vulnerability was first exploited fell from 53 days to 25 days, and to 8 days in the second quarter of 2026.
  • A new BSI "Cyber Index", which the agency uses to summarise the threat level, averaged 170 points, which the BSI describes as a rise of 50 percent.

The agency says small and medium-sized businesses and local authorities are especially exposed, and that fewer than half of users apply basic security measures.

BSI President Claudia Plattner said the agency is dealing with tools that allow cyber attacks in previously unknown volumes and at previously unknown speeds (our translation from the German press release).

AI agents as the next step

At the press conference, according to the German public broadcaster ZDF, Ms Plattner said the BSI expects attacks carried out by autonomously acting AI agents to increase in the next stage. Reuters, as carried by The News, also reported that the BSI warned agentic AI gives attackers more ways in. The written press release itself does not mention AI agents.

Mr Dobrindt said in the release that entry points for attackers are growing as the use of AI increases, and referred to a large cyber security package with new capabilities and powers. The release does not say what the package will contain or when it will be presented.

What is not yet known

The press release does not set out how much of the faster exploitation the BSI attributes to AI tools, compared with other causes. Reports of the event also give some figures that differ from the BSI's own; this story uses the BSI's figures. The details of the government's planned security package are not public.

Why it matters for people staying in charge

When flaws are exploited within days, the products most at risk are those that stop receiving updates, or that update slowly. That applies to AI assistants and agents as much as to connected devices and robots. A home robot or AI agent that someone else has taken control of is one nobody is in charge of.

Two of the Humasure Directives speak directly to this. D6 Secure and supported is about protection against attack and timely security fixes. D10 Safe for its whole life is about that care continuing for as long as people use the product. D9 Accountable is about someone answering when something goes wrong.

For practical questions to ask a maker about updates and security support, see Humasure's security page.
